findings.claim: Ruling (b) puts a new HEAD-based ignore check in 'the run-start guard', and the designs leave it no legal place to live: in gauntlet-run/scripts/guard.ts it is a second statement of the working-folder check and its messages, which :281 forbids (plan-review-design.md:430 and spec-review-design.md:525 forbid 'any other check of gauntlet/ being ignored'); in .shared/working-folder.ts it is no longer a run-start check, which gauntlet-design.md:132 forbids, and it then binds every caller.
findings.failure_scenario: Case 1: the implementer adds the check plus a 'commit it' message to gauntlet-run/scripts/guard.ts, beside requireIgnored(). Two statements of the ignore check now exist, which the Homes rows forbid, and the fence or reviewer flags it. Case 2: the implementer moves it into requireIgnored(). Then standalone intake, plan-review and spec-review run in the checkout and never cut a tree. They refuse an owner whose gauntlet/ line is ignored but not yet committed, with the message 'commit it'. That is a stop on a non-issue (CLAUDE.md 1.4). Either way a design line breaks.

findings.claim: Ruling (b) accepts only HEAD's .gitignore or .git/info/exclude, so it drops the global excludes file that :57 counts, though a tree run as the same user on the same host also honours that file. This is the same over-refusal the D-54 ruling (CONTEXT.md:71) rejected for a config 'that may reach the tree'.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner puts gauntlet/ in ~/.config/git/ignore (core.excludesFile) and has no repo-level line. The tree guard, requireIgnored() run in the Archon worktree, would pass because git reads the same global excludes there. The new run-start check refuses anyway and tells the owner to commit a line, so the run stops before any phase over a setup that works.

findings.claim: No git query reports ignore rules as committed at HEAD: git check-ignore reads only working-tree .gitignore files. So 'requires the ignore line in HEAD's .gitignore' must be built as a text match on `git show HEAD:.gitignore`, outside git's matcher. That contradicts the 'passes when git reports gauntlet/ ignored' semantics at gauntlet-intake-design.md:56. A git-native alternative exists: working-copy check-ignore plus `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .gitignore`.
findings.failure_scenario: Rejects a working setup: HEAD's .gitignore holds `/gauntlet`, `gauntlet` or `gauntlet/*`. Each makes git ignore the folder in the tree, but a literal `gauntlet/` line match refuses the run. Accepts a broken one: HEAD holds `gauntlet/` and a later `!gauntlet/`. The text match passes, then the tree's requireIgnored() fails after intake, plan review and spec review are paid for. That is the G-80 defect left standing.
